name: Porterfield Collegiate / Flyabout (CP-50, CP-65, LP-65)
summary: Prewar two-seat high-wing trainers and sport planes from Kansas City. The Collegiate is nicknamed the 'Skinny Bird' for its very narrow fuselage.

wings: High wing braced by two parallel struts per side (not a V)
Nearly symmetrical airfoil, straight wing with rounded tips
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long glazed roof
Fixed gear with a tailwheel or tailskid
tail: Conventional fin and rudder with a high-set fixed tailplane

tellTales: Light-plane-sized high-wing with two parallel struts per side instead of a V
Tandem seats under a long glazed roof

confusedWith.howToTell: The J-3 has V-struts and a rounder, wider fuselage; the Porterfield has parallel struts and a skinny slab-sided body.
The Champ has V-struts and a rounded teardrop fuselage; the Porterfield has parallel struts and a narrow slab-sided fuselage.
The Taylorcraft has side-by-side seats and V-type bracing; the Porterfield has tandem seats and twin parallel struts.
The Interstate Cadet has a V-strut braced wing and robust oleo gear; the Porterfield has paired parallel struts.
